newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen stabilising.

text.p: Polish shares rose on Wednesday after a steep three-session fall and analysts said that the market should begin to stabilise as it waits for data on the damage caused by the recent flooding in southern Poland.

"We've already had a reaction with those companies that are affected in a major way, we've had suspensions, we've had the decline....The worst is probably behind us (though) on balance it will be negative for the market," said Daiwa's Roger Monson.
Analysts also said investors would be watching to see to what degree Poland's planned 1997 budget deficit of 2.8 percent of GDP might be affected in the face of planned flood relief.
On Wednesday the finance minister said the planned 2.5-billion-zloty flood relief credit from the central bank would not increase total budgetary spending in 1997.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.1 percent to 15,268.4 points and turnover rose 5.3 percent to 207.5 million zlotys ($59.6 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 80 to 16 with 11 stocks flat.
Analysts said the stronger buying after price fixing could signal another gain on Thursday as the stabilisation begins.
Copper firm KGHM rose 9.7 percent on Wednesday, a natural rebound after having fallen about 10 percent during each of the last two sessions in profit taking, analysts said.
They said KGHM, which saw strong selling after fixing, may have benefited from the zloty's five-percent fall on Tuesday as its costs are largely in zlotys, its revenues in dollars.

Analysts said Tuesday's news cement firm Gorazdze sustained no damage from the flooding in southern Poland helped it rise 9.6 percent on Wednesay, along with perceived higher future demand for cement.
